key_behaviors: Phase 1 is NEVER skipped, even for a service that looks simple
Sub-agents (discovery-analyst, spec-analyst) MUST run in their own isolated context; a failed dispatch is a COMPLETION-BUG that STOPS the run — the orchestrator never self-runs the work
Generation spec MUST resolve and be PASTED verbatim; if no spec resolves, STOP — never substitute the reference service or CLAUDE.md descriptions
Every DB identifier in the migrated data-access layer is byte-for-byte identical to legacy (no renaming/casing/pluralization)
Legacy behavior-spec.json is committed first and is immutable; any later modification is a CI-detected tampering signal
Parity gate is fail-closed: exit 2 is TERMINAL for the agent — it may propose an override in parity-override-requested but NEVER writes parity-clean; only a human clears it
Coverage floor (default 85%) is met by ADDING TESTS ONLY — production code is never mutated/excluded to game the number
Name-contract items must each resolve to IMPLEMENTED or explicitly NOT REACHABLE (reachability traced from the migrated entry point) — no silent listed-but-unimplemented items
Phase-2 code-complete is NOT done: must invoke fix-and-close, run Stage 1, push, and open the PR before reporting complete
PR opens with explicit --repo <canonical> so it never lands against the legacy production repo; never force-push, never merge, one service per PR, legacy repo read-only

Target platform is .NET 10 per the shipped generation spec (dotnet-service.md) and the dotnet-version: 10.x in the CI template; no other target was named

This runs in an installed consumer repo (.claude/ tree present), NOT inside code-forge itself — 'migrate the account service' is a consumer-side invocation, so I'd resolve FRAMEWORK_ROOT to <project>/.claude
The base/remote branch and migrationPrefix come from config (no hardcoded 'main'); the CI template's AccountLookUp_POC target-branch suggests this team's base may not be main
Running attended enough to clear the single Phase 1 human gate; if unattended, I'd stop at that gate and at any parity exit-2 rather than self-authorize

The service touches a SQL Server DB (typical for these CTI services), so name-contract + extraction scripts + WIRE-B are all in scope; if discovery finds no DB access, those steps degrade to the documented minimal-artifact path
